Here's why... 🧵", "quote_tweet_id": "1453828617121234945" } Example - Reply to a tweet: { "text": "Great point! Here's my take on this...", "reply_in_reply_to_tweet_id": "1453828617121234945" }

params.name: text
params.description: Text content of the Tweet. Length limits are enforced by the X (Twitter) API and depend on the authenticated user's account tier — basic accounts are typically capped at 280 weighted characters (emojis/CJK count as 2, URLs count as 23 regardless of length), while X Premium accounts may post longer content. Validation is delegated to the API; over-length submissions return a 4xx error. At least one of `text`, `media_media_ids`, `card_uri`, `poll_options`, or `quote_tweet_id` must be provided with a non-empty value. Empty strings or whitespace-only strings are not valid. IMPORTANT: Do not include t.co URLs (Twitter's URL shortener) - use original URLs and Twitter will shorten them automatically. Also avoid URL placeholders like <URL>, [URL], or {URL} which will be rejected.

params.name: card_uri
params.description: URI of a card to attach. Mutually exclusive with `quote_tweet_id`, `poll` parameters, `media` parameters, and `direct_message_deep_link`.

params.name: nullcast
params.description: Marks the Tweet as a promoted-only post, not appearing in public timelines or served to followers.

params.name: geo_place_id

params.description: List of 2 to 4 poll options (max 25 characters each). Required if creating a poll. Mutually exclusive with `card_uri`.

params.name: quote_tweet_id
params.description: ID of the Tweet to quote. MUST be a numeric string containing only digits (1-19 digits). Accepts string or numeric types, automatically converted to string. Example: '1346889436626259968' is valid. Placeholder values like 'unknown', 'null', 'none' are NOT valid. Mutually exclusive with `card_uri`, `poll` parameters, and `direct_message_deep_link`.

params.name: reply_settings

params.name: media_media_ids

Example: '1455952740635586573' is valid, 'PLACEHOLDER_MEDIA_ID' is invalid. At least one of `text` or `media_media_ids` must be provided. Mutually exclusive with `card_uri`.

params.name: poll_reply_settings
params.description: Per X's live TweetCreateRequest schema (poll.reply_settings), all 4 values are valid - the same set as the top-level reply_settings enum, plus 'verified' (confirmed via api.x.com/2/openapi.json).

params.name: media_tagged_user_ids
params.description: User IDs to tag in media; tagged users must have enabled photo tagging. Mutually exclusive with `card_uri`.

params.name: poll_duration_minutes
params.description: Poll duration in minutes (5-10080). Required if `poll_options` are provided. Mutually exclusive with `card_uri`.

params.name: direct_message_deep_link

params.name: for_super_followers_only

params.name: reply_in_reply_to_tweet_id

Example: '1346889436626259960' is valid, 'Hello' is invalid. Required if creating a reply. Note: Twitter does not allow replies to tweets that have been edited - use quote_tweet_id instead for edited tweets.

params.name: reply_exclude_reply_user_ids

tools.title: Search full archive of tweets
tools.description: Searches the full archive of public Tweets from March 2006 onwards, with optional time bounds. Search queries are normalized, and parseable time bounds outside the supported range are adjusted.

params.name: query
params.description: The search query or rule to match Tweets. Rules: (1) Must contain at least one positive term (word, hashtag, username, phrase) - queries with only negations (e.g. '-is:retweet') or only operators (e.g. 'lang:en') are invalid. (2) Spaces act as implicit AND (e.g. 'cat dog' finds both). Do NOT use the word 'AND' - causes 'Ambiguous use of and' errors. (3) Uppercase OR for OR logic (e.g. 'cat OR dog'). (4) '-' prefix for NOT (e.g. '-retweet'). (5) Parentheses for grouping (e.g. '(cat OR dog) photo'). (6) Wildcards (*) are NOT supported. (7) Standalone '#' is invalid - hashtags need text after '#'. (8) '&' is auto-converted to space. (9) Context annotations: 'context:domain_id.entity_id' filters by X's auto-detected topics/entities (e.g. 'context:12.706083845846597632' for LA Lakers) - only valid domain-entity pairs work; invalid IDs cause 'Invalid Domain-Entity pair specified' errors.

params.name: end_time

If provided time is too recent, it will be automatically adjusted to 10 seconds before the request time. Example: '2021-01-31T23:59:59Z'.

params.description: Specifies which objects to expand in the response for more details.

params.description: Specifies the order in which to return results. 'recency' returns the most recent Tweets first, 'relevancy' returns Tweets based on relevance.

If provided time is before this minimum date, it will be automatically adjusted to 2006-03-21T00:00:00Z. Example: '2021-01-01T00:00:00Z'.
